data.narrative:
JITX is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $12M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of nine companies—one public and eight private—spanning seed through Series B stages in robotics and manufacturing, including comparable-stage entrants like Humanoid ($1.4B Series A) and growth-stage peers like Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B) and Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses total raised ($12M) as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A-to-next-stage advancement, implying a valuation of $24M. The peer-median method examines the five robotics and manufacturing companies at same or adjacent stages, yielding a median valuation of $1.6B with a range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics, seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B).

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range: $20.4M (low), $837M (median), and $1.9B (high). The stage-progression result sits substantially below peer medians, reflecting the tension between JITX's early-stage position and recent market valuations of robotics peers. Key uncertainties include the composition of the peer set—notably the presence of later-stage Series B valuations and the absence of publicly traded direct comparables—and whether peer valuations reflect sustainable fundamentals or sector-wide inflation. Additional diligence on unit economics, customer traction, and technology differentiation would be needed to narrow this range meaningfully.
